subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Work done by a constant force is calculated as:
questions.explain: Work = force x distance moved in the direction of the force.

questions.q: A 10 N force moves an object 3.0 m in the direction of the force. The work done is:
Kinetic energy is given by:
questions.explain: Kinetic energy depends on mass and the square of speed.

questions.q: A 2.0 kg object moves at 3.0 m/s. Its kinetic energy is:
Gravitational potential energy near Earth's surface is:
questions.explain: GPE = mass x g x height above a reference level.

questions.q: Lifting a 5.0 kg mass 2.0 m (g = 9.8 m/s^2) increases its GPE by about:
The principle of conservation of energy states that energy:
options: Cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred
questions.explain: Total energy is constant; it changes form (e.g. GPE to KE) rather than being lost.

questions.q: A ball of mass m falls from rest through height h. Ignoring air resistance, its speed on landing is:
questions.explain: Energy conservation: mgh = 0.5mv^2, so v = sqrt(2gh).

questions.q: Power is defined as:
options: The rate of doing work (energy transferred per unit time)
questions.explain: Power P = work/time, measured in watts.

questions.q: A motor does 6000 J of work in 30 s. Its power output is:
A car engine provides 5000 N of force at a constant 20 m/s. Its power output is:
Efficiency is calculated as:
options: Useful output energy divided by total input energy
Total energy divided by useful energy
questions.explain: Efficiency (often as a percentage) compares useful output with total input.

questions.q: A machine takes in 800 J and delivers 600 J of useful work. Its efficiency is:
questions.explain: Efficiency = 600/800 x 100 = 75%.

questions.q: When a force is perpendicular to the direction of motion, the work it does is:
questions.explain: W = Fs cos(90) = 0; a centripetal force, for example, does no work.

questions.q: Elastic potential energy stored in a stretched spring is:
questions.explain: Elastic PE = half x spring constant x extension squared.

questions.q: A spring (k = 200 N/m) is stretched 0.10 m. The elastic PE stored is:
At the bottom of a frictionless swing, a pendulum's energy is mostly:
questions.explain: GPE is converted to KE, which is maximum at the lowest point of the swing.

questions.q: A 1200 kg car brakes from 20 m/s to rest. The kinetic energy dissipated is:
In a real machine, output energy is less than input energy because some is:
options: Transferred to the surroundings, often as heat
questions.explain: Energy is dissipated (e.g. by friction) as thermal energy, reducing efficiency below 100%.

questions.q: Hooke's law states that (within the limit) the extension of a spring is:
questions.explain: F = kx: extension is directly proportional to force up to the elastic limit.
